extra.message: OS Command Injection in course_shell_probe_634: The 'host' parameter from request.GET is directly concatenated into shell command via _os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands via host=;cat /etc/passwd

Path Traversal in course_vault_stash_245: The 'ref' parameter from request.GET is used directly in file path construction (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json'). An attacker can use ref=../../etc/passwd to access or write arbitrary files.

Path Traversal in course_dock_shelf_593: The 'name' parameter from request.GET is used directly in file path construction (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name). An attacker can use name=../../../etc/passwd to write arbitrary files to the filesystem.

Template Injection (Code Injection) in course_jinja_cast_586: User input from 'fragment' GET parameter is passed directly to Jinja2 Template and rendered. An attacker can access internal variables, execute arbitrary code, or read sensitive files via fragment={{...}} syntax.

XML External Entities (XXE) in course_xml_fold_616: The lxml XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This allows XXE attacks where an attacker can read local files, perform SSRF attacks, or cause denial of service via billion laughs attack.

Open Redirect in course_return_lane_162: The 'lane' parameter from request.GET or request.POST is passed directly to redirect() without validation. An attacker can redirect users to external malicious sites via lane=https://evil.com.

Sensitive Data Exposure in course_vault_stash_245: SSN and credit card numbers are accepted via GET parameters (ssn, card) and stored to file without encryption. This exposes PII and PCI data in logs and the filesystem.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Hardcoded Credentials in seed_demo.py: Password 'DemoPass123!' and API key 'lms_demo_admin_api_key_for_local_checks' are hardcoded. If this code is used in production or the key is not changed, attackers can use these credentials to gain unauthorized access.

Insecure Default SECRET_KEY in settings.py: The Django SECRET_KEY defaults to 'local-dev-insecure-change-me' when the environment variable is not set. If deployed with this default, session tokens and other cryptographic signatures can be easily forged.

Debug Mode Enabled by Default in settings.py: DEBUG defaults to True. This exposes detailed error pages, stack traces, and internal application details in production, helping attackers understand the application structure.

CORS Misconfiguration in course_origin_mirror_564: The 'origin' header from the request is reflected in Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This allows cross-origin requests with credentials to any origin, enabling CSRF attacks.

Unbounded Resource Consumption in course_nonce_roll_604: The 'length' parameter from request.GET defaults to 24 but has no maximum limit. An attacker can specify length=999999999 to cause excessive memory allocation and CPU usage, leading to denial of service.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: Insecure Deserialization in course_preflet_roll_065: The JSON body from the request is decoded and then directly used to update the 'workset' dictionary which is returned to the user. While not a traditional deserialization vulnerability (since JSON is safe), this endpoint accepts and returns arbitrary JSON data structures which could be used in conjunction with other vulnerabilities.

Insecure SSL/TLS Configuration in course_trust_drift_644: The code uses ssl._create_unverified_context() which disables SSL certificate verification. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks when connecting to the partner endpoint.
